title: Choose Grădina Kasper’s visual world
question: Which world should become the durable identity for the homepage and the rest of the storefront?

options.label: The Kitchen Table Planner
options.lineage: family meal planners, fridge magnets, and handwritten weekly lists
options.thesis: The store feels like a friendly weekly ritual: see what the greenhouse packed, choose a box, and know when it arrives.
options.viewport: A calm navigation sits above a bold two-part opening: a human greenhouse photograph and an oversized featured-box planner module with the add action always visible.
options.risk: The magnet language becomes childish if every element performs; photography and disciplined spacing must keep it grown-up.

raised.raise: The opening inherits typographic scale courage without the shouting or diagonal chaos.
One unmistakable featured-box focal moment leads every viewport.
Availability, fulfillment date, and cart state use a strict, instantly readable status language.
Transitions feel organic and continuous while the content remains still and legible.

options.label: The Greenhouse Packing Table
options.lineage: produce crates, packing slips, greenhouse bench tags, and inked harvest stamps
options.thesis: Visitors arrive at the packing table: every box is visibly assembled by the people who grew it.
options.viewport: A wide greenhouse-and-packing photograph carries the first viewport while a large rounded order ticket presents the featured box, contents, next date, price, and add action.
options.risk: This is the most familiar grounded direction and could become generic farmers-market branding if the packing system is not executed precisely.

options.label: The Sunlit Greenhouse Section
options.lineage: architectural daylight sections translated into a working greenhouse
options.thesis: One continuous greenhouse section follows morning light from growing rows to a finished vegetable box.
options.viewport: The homepage opens as a broad greenhouse cutaway: people tend plants at one end and the featured box waits on a packing bench in the warm beam at the other.
options.case: Strong on the human greenhouse story and memorability; slightly weaker than the grounded directions at making the shop action immediate.
options.risk: It can read as an educational architecture experience before it reads as a vegetable-box store.

options.label: The Growing Word
options.lineage: an alphabet storm translated into type that sprouts and gathers
options.thesis: Large friendly words gather into boxes as the visitor moves through the page.
options.viewport: The offer is made through oversized type with one real product box anchoring the words.
options.case: The typography is memorable, but the metaphor obscures provenance and the actual catalogue.
options.kept: Responsive type should feel active rather than merely scaling down.
options.risk: The playful device overwhelms the greenhouse and risks becoming a novelty.

options.label: The Harvest Manifesto
options.lineage: wood-type manifesto slabs translated into bold harvest statements
options.thesis: The greenhouse promise and box names become a sequence of oversized green typographic slabs.
options.viewport: A huge promise fills one side while the featured box occupies one decisive rounded field.
options.case: Product clarity survives, but the aggressive rhythm conflicts with friendly, lightly playful restraint.
options.kept: The headline must have enough scale to give the small brand confidence.
options.risk: It would feel louder and more campaign-like than the ongoing household relationship needs.

options.label: The Long Green Shadow
options.lineage: two-ink one-sheets translated into a single greenhouse silhouette
options.thesis: A grower and vegetable box cast one dramatic green shadow that points toward the primary action.
options.viewport: One photographed figure and box form a strong diagonal toward the catalogue action.
options.case: The focal hierarchy is excellent, but the cinematic tension works against warmth and everyday trust.
options.kept: Every page needs one unmistakable focal moment rather than several equal card grids.
options.risk: The story feels dramatic and distant instead of open and neighborly.

options.label: The Floating Harvest
options.lineage: floated pigment translated into vegetable-color rings and soft transitions
options.thesis: Seasonal colors flow around a clean product box and reorganize as the catalogue changes.
options.viewport: A clean shop composition sits on one flowing field of vegetable color with a large featured box at center.
options.case: It feels organic and playful, but decoration competes with real photography and product distinctions.
options.kept: Motion should feel like one continuous natural displacement rather than scattered effects.
options.risk: It may imply artisan paper or cosmetics more readily than fresh produce.

options.label: The Harvest Event Display
options.lineage: particle-event notation translated into availability and contents data
options.thesis: Each box becomes a precise radial readout of contents, seasonality, and availability.
options.viewport: A featured box sits at the center of an exact contents-and-season readout.
options.case: State clarity is strong, but the scientific interface alienates household shoppers and obscures the human story.
options.kept: Availability and fulfillment status should be encoded with strict consistency.
options.risk: The store would feel analytical and synthetic rather than fresh and friendly.

canonCard.label: The Category Standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished farm-to-table shop with a green hero, clean product cards, and straightforward trust sections.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional split hero introduces the greenhouse and leads directly into a tidy featured-box card.
canonCard.risk: Clear and usable, but intentionally similar to many organic grocery storefronts.
